summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with a history of endometriosis and bipolar disorder was admitted for acute-on-chronic left lower quadrant pain radiating to the rectum and left leg, consistent with an endometriosis flare. Initial presentation included tachycardia and severe pain requiring IV analgesics. CT imaging showed a small hemorrhagic ovarian cyst but no acute surgical or infectious findings. Pain was controlled with IV then oral medications, including increased gabapentin and addition of tizanidine. She received a Lupron injection and was started on norethindrone for long-term management. The hospital course was uncomplicated, and she was discharged home on day two in stable condition with follow-up arranged.
